To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GridDBSCAN is a fast and exact parallel implementation of the popular clustering algorithm DBSCAN.

(a) GridDBSCAN, a new sequential algorithm, is 2-4 times faster than the state of the art sequential DBSCAN, and (b) its parallel implementations are 4-8 times faster than the best sequential algorithm, and 2-4x faster than the best parallel algorithm.
we present a grid based DBSCAN algorithm, which is significantly efficient, both sequentially and in parallel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a scalable and efficient DBSCAN algorithm that can be deployed for large data sets in commodity platforms.
the design of efficient and scalable parallel algorithms for density-based clustering.
the development of efficient, scalable parallel implementations of DBSCAN for commodity platforms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm is the fastest DBSCAN implementation to-date.
the proposed algorithms are faster than the state of the art sequential and parallel algorithms.
GridDBSCAN is an efficient and scalable parallel algorithm to cluster large data sets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GridDBSCAN and parallel GridDBSCAN are faster than state-of-the-art DBSCAN algorithms, without compromising on the quality of clusters, and they are exactly same as the classical sequential DBSCAN.
GridDBSCAN can be used as a drop-in replacement for DBSCAN, and its parallel implementations can be used as drop-in replacement for sequential DBSCAN on commodity clusters.
GridDBSCAN can cluster a large data set with a million points within 1.5 hours on a commodity cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GridDBSCAN and parallel GridDBSCAN are significantly faster than the classical sequential DBSCAN and the state-of-the art parallel DBSCAN algorithms.
the performance improvements of GridDBSCAN are achieved by exploiting spatial locality information and by using a simple grid-based index structure.
GridDBSCAN can be used as a replacement of classical DBSCAN in large data mining problems.
